title: Merchants turn the temple into business — John 2
paragraphs: Merchants turn the temple into business — John 2
He didn’t lose His temper.
He revealed His holiness.

In John 2, Jesus walked into the temple and found a place meant for prayer turned into a marketplace. Worship had been buried under profit. Sacrifice had been wrapped in convenience. Holy things were being used for selfish gain.
And Christ would not stay silent.

He made a whip.
He overturned tables.
He drove them out.
Why?

Because God’s house was never meant to be a stage for greed.
Never meant to be a machine for exploitation.
Never meant to make people rich while pretending to bring people near to God.
But here’s what we miss.

This story is not only about them.
It’s about us.

How often do we dress up ambition in spiritual language?
How often do we use worship for attention, ministry for ego, religion for gain?
How often do we look holy outside while our hearts are bargaining inside?
Jesus still walks into temples.
And now, by His Spirit, we are that temple.

So when He flips tables, He is not being cruel.
He is being merciful.
He is driving out what is defiling what He loves.

That’s the Gospel.
Jesus does not cleanse the temple to destroy it.
He cleanses it so His presence can dwell there rightly.
He confronts sin, exposes corruption, and then goes to the cross for the very people who polluted what was holy.
The same Jesus who overturned tables would soon have His own body broken for sinners.
For us.

So let Him search you.
Let Him cleanse you.
Let Him tear down every hidden idol of greed, pride, performance, and hypocrisy.
Because the hands that overturn tables are the same hands that were pierced for your redemption.
He is not trying to shame you. He is trying to free you.
